Transport Modes

Plattformcontainer

A reinforced flat platform without side or end walls, used to transport oversized, heavy, or unconventional cargo that cannot fit in standard or closed containers.

Quick answer: A reinforced flat platform without side or end walls, used to transport oversized, heavy, or unconventional cargo that cannot fit in standard or closed containers.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Plattformcontainer?

In this glossary, Plattformcontainer refers to: A reinforced flat platform without side or end walls, used to transport oversized, heavy, or unconventional cargo that cannot fit in standard or closed containers.

How is Plattformcontainer used in logistics?

In logistics communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Plattformcontainer sind ideal für den Transport von Ladungen, die die Längen-, Breiten- oder Gewichtsbeschränkungen von Standardcontainern überschreiten."

Why does Plattformcontainer matter in logistics?

Plattformcontainer matters because it supports clear communication in Transport Modes contexts for Freight Forwarders, Supply Chain Managers, and Customs Brokers. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as FIATA Diploma, CILT Certification, and IATA DGR.

Who uses Plattformcontainer?

Plattformcontainer is mainly used by Freight Forwarders, Supply Chain Managers, and Customs Brokers.

What category does Plattformcontainer belong to?

In this glossary, Plattformcontainer is grouped under Transport Modes. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from Incoterms 2020 (ICC), FIATA, IATA DGR, WCO and published by Protermify Logistics as a static logistics reference page.

Definition

A reinforced flat platform without side or end walls, used to transport oversized, heavy, or unconventional cargo that cannot fit in standard or closed containers.

Operational example

Platform containers are ideal for transporting cargo that exceeds the length, width, or weight restrictions of standard containers.

Localized term
